gaps: P0: none; P3: none; P5–P6: none usable (#13 is the airfield, #17 a garden wall, #14–#16 other places)
notes: #4 carries the title of Silvestre’s series “Profil de la ville de Nancy, auquel sont jointes les veuës et perspectives des portes…”; the Rijksmuseum dates another plate of the same series (#6) to 1650, so I dated it about 1650 instead of its loose 1620–64 range. #1 is a perspective plan rather than a view (houses drawn in the old town, blocks in the new town); #2 and #3 are bound copies of the same plate and #7 an 1880s reproduction. #5 (Callot copy, “in or after 1635”) is a nice skyline view but its date is too loose. #10 (1891–96, panorama from Saint-Epvre with the cathedral) is a good alternative to #11. #8 is a whaling boat named Nancy Grey, #15–#16 a Dieppe painting in Nancy’s museum.
